is_error_case_convention: is_error_case is true only for a criterion whose expected outcome is an Err return, a panic, or a compile failure. It is false for every criterion whose expected outcome is an Ok/success value, even when that value represents a degenerate, empty, or non-finite input (e.g. a 0-member LiteralUnion, a NaN payload, or an unrecognized-but-parseable tag) — those are edge-case success criteria, not error criteria. No single criterion may bundle an Err outcome and an Ok outcome under one flag — where a method has both an error path and a related success path (e.g. PropType::from_tagged_value's absent/non-string-kind Err versus its unrecognized-but-parseable-kind Ok), each outcome is its own criterion. Applied uniformly: AC-001, AC-004C, and AC-004E are the only criteria carrying true.
purpose: Define the construction-time and serialization contract for the shared output types (PropType, CollectedType, ComponentEntry, ParsedProp, Diagnostic) in crates/core::types so that every downstream consumer (RDT-compat JSON, Storybook, TOON, JSON Schema, the msgpack DTS cache) reads a tree that cannot be constructed in a contradictory required/default state and that round-trips faithfully through JSON, including non-finite float literals. This contract governs the ParsedProp::new construction path and serialization only; it does not guarantee the invariant survives post-construction field mutation (AC-014B) or deserialization via the derived serde impl (AC-014C) — both are named, decided exceptions, not silent gaps.
scope: crates/core/src/types/output.rs (PropType, ComponentEntry, ParsedProp, OpaqueDetail, OpaqueReason) and crates/core/src/types/collected.rs (CollectedType) and crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs (Diagnostic, DiagnosticSeverity, DiagnosticCode) — their public construction API and their JSON serialize/deserialize behavior, including malformed-input handling.
non_goals: The specific serialized shape of any one output format (RDT-compat, Storybook, TOON, JSON Schema) — those are separate capabilities that consume this contract, not part of it.

How the resolver decides what value to put into these types (e.g. which OpaqueReason to pick, how a discriminated union is detected, library-specific shortcuts in known.rs that call OpaqueDetail::new directly) — that is the resolver's contract, not this one's.
The msgpack cache's own (de)serialization format for SourceData — this spec covers the JSON contract of the output types only, not cache.rs's separate encoding.

Preventing post-construction mutation of ParsedProp's public required/default_value fields, or deserialization via #[derive(Deserialize)], from re-introducing the contradictory state — both are pub/derived and reachable without going through ParsedProp::new; the sealed constructor only guarantees the invariant at the moment of construction through new (see AC-014B, AC-014C). Closing either hole (private fields with accessors, or a manual Deserialize impl that re-normalizes) is a separate, not-yet-decided design change.

ObjectField's construction/serialization contract — it has no default_value field and cannot represent the required/default contradiction this spec is about; its serialization is already exercised indirectly wherever a PropType::Object value round-trips under AC-004.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A `ParsedProp { name: ..., prop_type: ..., .. }` bare struct literal, written in a module outside crates/core/src/types/output.rs (including another module in the same crate), fails to compile because the private `_seal: Seal` field cannot be named or constructed from outside that module.

Calling `ParsedProp::new(name: String, prop_type: PropType, required: bool, default_value: Option<DefaultValue>, description: String, tags: BTreeMap<String, String>, parent: Option<PropParent>, declarations: Vec<PropParent>)` (this exact positional order) with `required = true` and `default_value = Some(dv)` for any `dv: DefaultValue` returns a `ParsedProp` whose `.required` field is `false`, regardless of the `true` passed for `required`.

Calling `ParsedProp::new(...)` (same positional signature as AC-002) with `required = true` and `default_value = None` returns a `ParsedProp` whose `.required` field is `true` — the normalization in AC-002 only fires when `default_value` is `Some(_)`, and does not force `required` to `false` unconditionally.

`PropType` (crates/core/src/types/output.rs) does not derive `serde::Serialize`/`serde::Deserialize` via `#[derive(...)]`; both traits are implemented by hand (`impl serde::Serialize for PropType`, `impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for PropType`) delegating to the private `to_tagged_value`/`from_tagged_value` methods, which build/parse a `serde_json::Value` directly. Serializing any `PropType` value via `serde_json::to_value` and deserializing the result back via `serde_json::from_value` returns `Ok` with a value equal to the original, except where any `PropType::NumberLiteral` node reachable within the value — at the top level, or nested inside `Union`, `Intersection`, `Array`, `Tuple`, `Object` (via a contained `ObjectField.prop_type`), or `Named`'s `args` — holds a NaN payload: for such a value the round-trip is still `Ok` and every such payload is still `is_nan()` (per AC-006, which establishes the top-level case; the same string-tagging mechanism applies uniformly regardless of nesting position since it operates node-by-node), but `==` comparison against the original is excluded because `f64::NAN != f64::NAN` (malformed-input cases are covered separately by AC-004C and AC-004C2).

`CollectedType` (crates/core/src/types/collected.rs) does not derive `serde::Serialize`/`serde::Deserialize` via `#[derive(...)]`; both traits are implemented by hand (`impl serde::Serialize for CollectedType`, `impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for CollectedType`) delegating to the private `to_json_value`/`from_json_value` methods, which build/parse a `serde_json::Value` directly.
Calling `PropType::from_tagged_value` on a `serde_json::Value` that is a JSON object whose `"kind"` field is absent, or present but not a JSON string, returns `Err`.

Calling `PropType::from_tagged_value` on an object whose `"kind"` field is a string that does not match any recognized tag (e.g. `{"kind": "bogus"}`) does NOT return `Err` — it returns `Ok(pt)` where `matches!(pt, PropType::Opaque(_))` is true, and for the contained detail (accessed via the `pub(crate)` accessors, from any module in the crate) `detail.raw() == "unknown PropType kind: bogus"` and `detail.reason() == &OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded`.

Calling `CollectedType::from_json_value` on a JSON number, bool, or null, and on a JSON object matching none of the recognized shape keys (`sl`, `nl`, `bl`, `n`, `u`, `i`, `arr`, `tup`, `obj`, `to`, `keyof`, `ia`, `tl`, `fn`, `cond`, `mapped`, `raw`), returns `Ok(CollectedType::Raw(v.to_string()))`, where `v.to_string()` is the input value's own JSON text.

Calling `CollectedType::from_json_value` on a JSON string returns `Ok`: for each of the eleven strings `"str"`, `"num"`, `"bool"`, `"null"`, `"undef"`, `"any"`, `"never"`, `"unknown"`, `"void"`, `"bigint"`, `"symbol"`, it returns the correspondingly-named unit variant (e.g. `"str"` -> `CollectedType::String`, `"symbol"` -> `CollectedType::Symbol`); for any other string `s` (e.g. `"foo"`), it returns `Ok(CollectedType::Raw(s))` — the string's own contents, with no surrounding JSON quotes (i.e. not `v.to_string()`, which would include the quotes).

Calling `CollectedType::from_json_value(&serde_json::json!({"obj": [1]}))` returns `Err`, because the element `1` inside the `"obj"` array is not a JSON object and the `obj`-array field-parsing arm requires each element to be an object.

`OpaqueReason` (crates/core/src/types/output.rs) carries `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` directly and no manual `impl Serialize`/`impl Deserialize` exists for it anywhere in the crate. That derived encoding is not, however, the wire format `OpaqueReason` actually takes when it appears inside a serialized `PropType::Opaque` value: `PropType::to_tagged_value`'s `Opaque` arm hand-builds the reason as `{"type": <camelCase variant tag>, ...payload fields in camelCase}` — e.g. `OpaqueReason::RuntimeDependent { function_name }` serializes as `{"type": "runtimeDependent", "functionName": function_name}`, and the unit variant `OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded` serializes as `{"type": "depthExceeded"}` — which differs from what `serde_json::to_value` on a bare `OpaqueReason` would produce via its own derived impl (serde's default externally-tagged form, e.g. `{"runtimeDependent": {"function_name": ...}}`). No expression of type `OpaqueReason` itself (as opposed to a type that merely contains one, such as `PropType`, `ParsedProp`, `ComponentEntry`, or `ExtractionOutput` — serializing those is expected and does not violate this criterion, because `PropType::to_tagged_value` intercepts the reason before serde ever sees a bare `OpaqueReason`) is ever passed directly to `serde_json::to_value`, `serde_json::to_string`, `rmp_serde::to_vec`, or a manual `Serialize::serialize` call anywhere in crates/core OUTSIDE a `#[cfg(test)]` module — verified by inspecting every file matching `grep -rl OpaqueReason crates/core/src` and confirming no serializer call outside a `#[cfg(test)]` module in any of them takes a bare `OpaqueReason` argument. (A `#[cfg(test)]` test proving this exact claim necessarily constructs a bare `OpaqueReason` and passes it to `serde_json::to_value` once, specifically to demonstrate that its derived encoding differs from `to_tagged_value`'s hand-built wire form — the criterion's own point — which is why the carve-out is scoped to test code, not production code.)

Serializing `PropType::NumberLiteral(f64::NAN)` to `serde_json::Value` via `serde_json::to_value` and deserializing the result back via `serde_json::from_value` yields a `PropType::NumberLiteral(n)` where `n.is_nan()` is true — not silently replaced with `0.0`.

Serializing `PropType::NumberLiteral(f64::INFINITY)` (and, separately, `f64::NEG_INFINITY`) to `serde_json::Value` and back via `serde_json::to_value`/`serde_json::from_value` yields a `PropType::NumberLiteral(n)` where `n` equals the original infinite value exactly (`n == f64::INFINITY` or `n == f64::NEG_INFINITY` respectively), not `0.0`.
Serializing `PropType::NumberLiteral(42.5)` (a finite value) to `serde_json::Value` via `serde_json::to_value` and back via `serde_json::from_value` yields `PropType::NumberLiteral(42.5)` unchanged.
`PropType::LiteralUnion { members: vec![], has_default: false }.is_literal_union()` returns `false`.
`PropType::LiteralUnion { members: vec!["only".to_string()], has_default: false }.is_literal_union()` returns `false`.
`PropType::LiteralUnion { members: vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()], has_default: false }.is_literal_union()` returns `true`.

The `Diagnostic` struct (crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs) has these public fields, each with this exact type, and no other public fields: `severity: DiagnosticSeverity`, `message: String`, `file: Option<String>`, `line: Option<u32>`, `column: Option<u32>`, `help: Option<String>`, `code: DiagnosticCode`.

Serializing a `Diagnostic` to JSON via `serde_json::to_value` renders the `severity` field's enum value in camelCase (e.g. `DiagnosticSeverity::Error` serializes as the string `"error"`), while the `code` field's `DiagnosticCode` enum value serializes in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. `DiagnosticCode::InternalPanic` serializes as the string `"INTERNAL_PANIC"`, not `"internalPanic"`).

Serializing a `ComponentEntry` to JSON via `serde_json::to_value` renders its struct field names in camelCase — `display_name` as the key `"displayName"` and `file_path` as the key `"filePath"` — and serializing a `ParsedProp` renders `default_value` as the key `"defaultValue"` and renders the `prop_type` field under the key `"type"` (via `#[serde(rename = "type")]`, not the struct's `rename_all = "camelCase"`, which would otherwise have produced `"propType"`).

Every call to `OpaqueDetail::give_up(state, raw, reason, diagnostic)` pushes the passed `diagnostic` onto `state.diagnostics` before returning the constructed `PropType::Opaque` value — verified by a test asserting `state.diagnostics.len()` increases by exactly 1 across the call and the pushed diagnostic equals what was passed in.

`ComponentEntry` (crates/core/src/types/output.rs) derives `serde::Serialize` and `serde::Deserialize` directly via `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` — it is not hand-serialized, and no manual impl of either trait exists for it anywhere in the crate. Serializing any `ComponentEntry` value via `serde_json::to_value` and deserializing the result back via `serde_json::from_value` returns `Ok` with a value equal to the original, except where any `PropType::NumberLiteral` node reachable from a contained `ParsedProp`'s `prop_type` — at the top level, or nested inside `Union`, `Intersection`, `Array`, `Tuple`, `Object` (via `ObjectField.prop_type`), or `Named`'s `args` — holds a NaN payload: for such a `ComponentEntry` the round-trip is still `Ok` and every such payload is still `is_nan()`, but `==` comparison against the original is excluded because `f64::NAN != f64::NAN` (same exception as AC-004, since ComponentEntry.props transitively contains PropType).

`ParsedProp`'s `required` and `default_value` fields are both `pub`. Given a `ParsedProp` value `prop` previously constructed via `ParsedProp::new("p".to_string(), PropType::String, true, Some(dv), String::new(), Default::default(), None, vec![])` for some `dv: DefaultValue` (which normalizes `prop.required` to `false` per AC-002), executing `prop.required = true;` in a test in the same crate compiles successfully and afterward leaves `prop.required == true` and `prop.default_value == Some(dv)` simultaneously — i.e. the contradictory state IS representable after construction via direct field mutation; only the `ParsedProp::new` constructor path is covered by AC-002's normalization guarantee.

`ParsedProp` derives `serde::Deserialize` via `#[derive(..., Deserialize)]` (with `_seal` marked `#[serde(skip)]`), and this derived impl performs no required/default_value normalization: deserializing a JSON object with `"required": true` and a non-null `"defaultValue"` (e.g. `serde_json::from_value::<ParsedProp>(serde_json::json!({"name": "p", "type": {"kind": "string"}, "required": true, "defaultValue": {"value": "a", "computed": false}, "description": "", "tags": {}, "parent": null, "declarations": []}))`) returns `Ok(prop)` where `prop.required == true` and `prop.default_value.is_some()` simultaneously — the sealed constructor's normalization guarantee (AC-002) does not extend to the deserialization path.
